system.specification_latex: The source system is expressed in the center-of-inertia coordinates $(\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3,\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3)$, which satisfy $\delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3=0$. We therefore remove the redundant common-angle coordinate and define $\delta_3:=-(\delta_1+\delta_2)$ and $\bar{\omega}:=\frac13(\omega_1+\omega_2+\omega_3)$. Let $\mathbf{x}=(\delta_1,\delta_2,\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3) \in\mathbb{R}^5$. The reduced vector field is \[ \dot{\mathbf{x}} = \begin{pmatrix} \dot{\delta}_1\\ \dot{\delta}_2\\ \dot{\omega}_1\\ \dot{\omega}_2\\ \dot{\omega}_3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} \omega_1-\bar{\omega}\\[0.4ex] \omega_2-\bar{\omega}\\[0.4ex] -\omega_1-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sin(\delta_1-\delta_j)\\[0.4ex] -\omega_2-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sin(\delta_2-\delta_j)\\[0.4ex] -\omega_3-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sin(\delta_3-\delta_j) \end{pmatrix}. \]
system.variant_postamble_latex: \begin{remark} The original system is stated in coordinates with $\delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3=0$. We substitute $\delta_3 := -(\delta_1+\delta_2)$ and impose $|\delta_1+\delta_2|\le0.75$ to eliminate the equilibrium line $\{(c,c,c,0,0,0)\}$ present in the six-dimensional formulation. This reduction makes the single-point stability problem well-defined. \end{remark}
